### Clarity Systems closes**$4.4 million** in seed funding to fight retail fraud  
*What it does:* Clarity Systems makes an X-ray and AI-powered scanner that inspects returned retail merchandise while still in its packaging. It aims to detect return fraud (counterfeits, swaps, missing parts) in real time without unpacking items.
*Why investors care:* Returns fraud is a massive hidden cost (\~$103B in 2024), and AI vision is a smart fix. The founders are retail veterans, and LMnT Ventures (formerly Lemonade’s incubator) led this $4.4M seed, joined by Regeneration VC, Humba Ventures, and Massive Technology Ventures. Though small, Clarity addresses a clear niche with defensible tech – akin to airport scanners but for boxes. High-profile pilot customers and the founder’s credibility helped attract funding. Investors likely see this as a first-mover in retail AI hardware.
*Why this round matters:* Clarity’s seed shows that even in a big-VC environment, there is room for practical AI startups tackling real pain points. For investors, an efficient returns solution can improve margins for major retailers, and per-scan pricing fees provide a recurring revenue stream. For founders, Clarity’s story illustrates that a targeted AI application (here, in logistics/retail) can close a significant seed round. If it succeeds, we may see more hardware+AI combos win early deals in domains like warehousing or industrial inspection.

# Clarity Systems' AI X-Ray Aims to Curb Retail's $103B Returns Fraud Crisis  
**SAN FRANCISCO, CA – August 13, 2026** – In a significant move to combat one of retail's most costly and fastest-growing challenges, fraud detection startup Clarity Systems has closed a $4.4 million seed funding round. The investment, led by early-stage venture firm LMnT Ventures, will accelerate the deployment of Clarity's novel system, which uses AI-powered X-ray technology to detect returns fraud in seconds without ever opening the box.  
The funding arrives as the retail industry grapples with staggering losses from fraudulent returns, a problem that has evolved far beyond simple shoplifting. “Retail fraud has become a professional industry, run at scale against the returns counter and the receiving dock, and most defenses were built for a shoplifting era,” said Andy Ruben, Cofounder and CEO of Clarity Systems. “We built Clarity to catch it the moment it enters the building.”  
Founded by retail and returns industry veterans Ruben, Darrell Whitelaw, and Sender Shamiss, Clarity Systems is positioning itself as a critical new line of defense. The new capital, with participation from Regeneration VC, Humba Ventures, and Massive Technology Ventures, validates the urgent market need for a smarter, more precise approach to loss prevention.
Within its first year, Clarity has already deployed its systems with major national retailers, demonstrating immediate traction and real-world applicability. As this technology becomes more widespread, it has the potential to set a new industry standard for how returns are managed, turning a major liability into a more secure and efficient operation. By giving retailers the ability to see the truth inside the box, Clarity Systems is bringing much-needed transparency to one of commerce's most opaque problems.

The Company’s system sees inside returned and received products in three seconds without having to manually open them - catching counterfeits, product swaps, and manipulation by comparing items or potential fraudulent items against the original manufacturer profile. AI-powered technology helps retailers detect returns fraud in three seconds or less without opening the box. Clarity enables retailers to verify the contents of returned and received products, without opening the package.
Similar to how an airport X-ray scanner identifies the contents of luggage without unpacking it, Clarity's system analyzes the product, and instantly detects anomalies such as counterfeit goods, product swaps, missing components, or other forms of return fraud.
